channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Skyway 2027: A Contemporary Collaboration
item.description: Triennial exhibition centering artists shaping contemporary art in the Tampa Bay region, co-organized by five museums: the Museum of Fine Arts St. Petersburg, The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art, Sarasota Art Museum of Ringling College, Tampa Museum of Art, and USF Contemporary Art Museum. Open to artists and collectives working in all media — photography included — who live in Hillsborough, Manatee, Pasco, Pinellas, or Sarasota counties. Selected artists exhibit at one of the five venues between March and fall 2027 and are featured in a full-color catalog with curatorial essays. Free to apply with up to 10 images (plus optional video). — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Fashion Regenerated 2026 · Textile Exchange
item.description: Photography and filmmaking competition from Textile Exchange, the global nonprofit driving sustainable fiber and material production, in partnership with Atmos. Visual storytellers are invited to document regeneration across the fashion, textile, and apparel industry — from fiber cultivation to circular design. The overall winner receives a $10,000 paid commission to create new work documenting regeneration, publication through Atmos and Textile Exchange, and an exhibition at the 2026 Textile Exchange Conference; two runners-up receive $2,000 each plus promotion and conference display. Open to photographers and filmmakers 18+ of any nationality; winners must be available to travel autumn 2026 – summer 2027 for the commission. Submit up to 25 photographs, a short film, or both. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 commission + Publication + Exhibition.

item.title: BBA 360 — Online Exhibition 2026
item.description: Open call from Berlin's BBA Gallery for its 360° digital exhibition format. Open to artists and photographers 18+ worldwide working in any medium except video and sculpture, with no theme restrictions. Around 45 artworks are featured in the immersive 360° online gallery; 15 shortlisted artists are additionally presented in an online group show with Artsy profiles and promotion through BBA channels. The first-prize winner receives a cash award, an Artsy profile, and a physical exhibition at BBA Gallery in Berlin in 2026/27. €29 fee covers up to 5 works; no shipping required for the online round. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: €29. Prize: Cash prize + Exhibition + Artsy profile.

item.title: Willet Art Prize 2026
item.description: Free national art competition from Willet Studios, the storied American stained glass studio founded in 1898. The 2026 theme, 'Quest for Gold,' invites work exploring movement, strength, determination, and the human pursuit of excellence in sport. Any medium is accepted and all experience levels are welcome — entries are judged on creativity, theme interpretation, composition, emotional impact, and suitability for translation into glass. Prizes of $7,000, $2,000, and $1,000 from a $10,000 total pool; winning designs may be developed into stained glass pieces with per-sale commissions to the artist for up to three years. One original work per artist, not previously exhibited. Open to US residents 18+; winners announced October 2026. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 prize pool.

item.title: EPF 2026 Photobook Exhibition · Ephemere
item.description: Open call for a dedicated photobook exhibition at the Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo (October 17–27), following the 118-title showcase Ephemere staged during KG+ in Kyoto. Seeking complete, bound photobooks — self-published or publisher-released, A4 or smaller — with bold visual narratives, intentional sequencing, and strong physical presence; theme is open. Two-phase system: the initial digital review is free (submit a PDF, flip-through video, or sequenced JPEGs of the book), then artists selected in July pay a $25 exhibition fee and ship one copy to Japan. Exhibited books are not returned — they join Ephemere's permanent traveling photo library and may be shown again at future international pop-ups. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free ($25 if selected). Prize: Exhibition in Tokyo + Traveling archive.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — September 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. Submission window for the September issue runs July 1–20, 2026; email submissions. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Minimalist Landscapes
item.description: Submit up to 5 minimalist landscape images with captions for the 'One Thing This Month' feature (OP 331) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives Nikon Action Zoom 10-22×50 binoculars (RRP £179). Captions up to 75 words with technical details (camera, lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture). Entries upload via Google Form. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Nikon binoculars (£179) + Publication.

item.title: Living Space — Artdoc Magazine Open Call · Artdoc Photography Magazine
item.description: Themed open call exploring the environments we inhabit and the spaces that shape everyday experience — cityscapes, rural landscapes, domestic interiors, architecture and the built environment, still lifes connected to daily life, and observations of ordinary surroundings. Open to photographers worldwide. Selected work may be featured in curated online exhibitions, the Featured Submissions page, or upcoming magazine issues, with possible interviews about the creative process. Submissions free for Artdoc Magazine members; non-members must subscribe to submit. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication / online exhibition.

item.title: 46th Arts of the Terrace Juried Art Show · Mountlake Terrace Friends of the Arts
item.description: Forty-sixth annual juried show presented by Mountlake Terrace Friends of the Arts at the Mountlake Terrace Library, just north of Seattle. Categories span paintings, printmaking, drawings, photography (film, digital, or altered images), 3-dimensional works, artisan works, and miniatures; open to artists 16+ with original work made in the past three years. Over $6,000 in prize money, including $500 first prizes per category and a $500 Best in Show chosen by the Arts Commission. Accepted work is hand-delivered September 11–12 (miniatures may be mailed by arrangement). On view September 19–26, 2026. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $20 per piece. Prize: $6,000+ in awards.

item.title: 2026 Virginia Artist Juried Exhibition · Charles H. Taylor Visual Arts Center
item.description: Annual statewide juried exhibition at Hampton Arts' Charles H. Taylor Visual Arts Center. Open to artists 18+ living or working in Virginia, with original work in any media created in the past two years and not previously shown at the center; up to three artworks per entry, max 60 inches in any direction. Juried by Ashley Millen, owner and director of Bond Millen Gallery in Richmond. Awards include $1,000 first place, $750 second, $500 third, and five $100 Awards of Distinction. On view September 19 – November 14, 2026. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $40 (members $35). Prize: $2,750 in awards.

item.title: Zion National Park Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description: Four-week residency living in the historic Grotto House in the main canyon of Zion National Park, Utah, run by the National Park Service with the Zion Forever Project. Three sessions are available across 2027. Includes rent-free furnished housing, waived park entrance fees, and a $500 stipend on completion of residency requirements. Open to artists 18+ in all mediums and skill levels; residents present two public programs, spend about 20 hours weekly on public engagement, and donate an original artwork to the park. Travel, meals, and supplies are self-funded; international applicants must be eligible for J-1 visa status. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: 4-week residency + Park housing + $500 stipend.

item.title: 2027 Grand Canyon Artist in Residence · Grand Canyon Conservancy
item.description: Four- to eight-week residency on the South Rim of Grand Canyon National Park, run by Grand Canyon Conservancy. Three artists are selected annually and receive an $800 weekly stipend, $500 travel subsidy, up to $300 for project supplies, free accommodation, special park access, and staff support, in exchange for roughly two public interactions per week. Open internationally to artists 18+ who are legally able to work in the US; priority for underrepresented perspectives and well-researched, Grand Canyon–specific projects. The application fee is waived for Indigenous artists from the canyon's 11 associated Tribal Nations. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $800/week stipend + Housing + Travel subsidy.

item.title: Villa Barr Art Park Artist in Residency 2027 · City of Novi
item.description: Three-month residencies (Spring, Summer, or Fall 2027) at Villa Barr Art Park, a four-acre former sculptor's estate run by the City of Novi, Michigan. Each session hosts a Visiting Artist living in the four-bedroom house plus a Local Artist with studio access; private and shared studios include woodworking and metalworking tools. All residents receive a $500 materials stipend, and Visiting Artists an additional $500 travel stipend. Open internationally to artists 18+; strong proposals engage the public through workshops, exhibitions, or installations responding to the grounds. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: 3-month residency + $500 stipend.

item.title: sƛ̓x̣etkʷ Artist-in-Residence Program — Round 3 · Spokane Falls Community College
item.description: Three-month winter residency (January 5 – March 26, 2027) at Spokane Falls Community College for emerging Native American artists who are enrolled members of a US federally recognized tribe, with priority for Pacific Northwest and Washington tribes, particularly the Schitsu'umsh (Coeur d'Alene). Offers a $9,000 stipend paid monthly, furnished off-campus housing, up to $500 travel reimbursement, access to fine-art facilities including ceramics, printmaking, digital art, and sculpture, and optional mentorship. Residents commit 35 hours weekly on campus; 'emerging' means without gallery representation. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $9,000 stipend + Housing + Studio access.

item.title: Lucid Art Residency 2027
item.description: Three-week residency in Inverness, California, on the edge of Point Reyes, founded in the lineage of surrealist painter Gordon Onslow Ford. Residents get a fully furnished house, the skylit Ark studio, optional water-based printmaking facilities, mentorship meetings with artist associates, and curation into an online exhibition of residency work. Open to US and Canadian artists 18+ with an MFA or equivalent and exhibition history, working in nonrepresentational styles across visual arts, eco-art, video, writing, music, or choreography; first-time applicants only. No stipend or meals, and a car is required. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: 3-week residency + Housing & studio.

item.title: SCG Artist in Residence & Teaching Program 2027 — Regional · Blue Line Arts
item.description: Three-week teaching residency (April 9–30, 2027) at Blue Line Arts in Roseville, California, funded by Placer Community Foundation. The selected artist receives a $10,000 honorarium plus $1,470 per diem and studio space, in exchange for an artist lecture, open studio hours, school tours, and two adult workshops. Open to artists 18+ residing in Placer, Nevada, Yolo, El Dorado, Sacramento, or Sutter-Yuba counties who have not previously held an SCG residency at Blue Line. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 honorarium + 3-week residency.

item.title: SCG Artist in Residence & Teaching Program 2027 — National · Blue Line Arts
item.description: Three-week teaching residency (August 13 – September 3, 2027) at Blue Line Arts in Roseville, California, funded by Placer Community Foundation. The selected artist receives a $10,000 honorarium, $1,470 per diem, up to $800 travel and $800 car-rental reimbursement, up to $4,200 housing reimbursement, and up to $500 for supplies and shipping. In exchange the artist gives a lecture, holds open studio hours, hosts school tours, and teaches two workshops. Open to US artists 18+ outside the six Northern California counties covered by the regional track. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 honorarium + Housing & travel covered.

item.title: Max Thelen Studio Residency · Art Works Downtown
item.description: Twelve-month free studio residency (September 2026 – August 2027) at Art Works Downtown in San Rafael, California, for an emerging visual artist with a committed early-to-mid-stage practice. Covers a 92 sq ft street-level studio with utilities, plus a solo exhibition, waived membership fees, social media promotion, and scholarship funding for Marin Open Studios participation. Applicants should live within commuting distance of San Rafael and work regularly in the studio. — Deadline: June 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 12-month free studio + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Hard Water, Soft Stone · Duplex AIR
item.description: September group exhibition at Duplex AIR, an artist-run studio, residency, and gallery space in Lisbon. The theme riffs on the Portuguese proverb about soft water breaking hard stone, inviting work on mutability, persistence, and slow transformation — misreadings and reinterpretations welcome. All mediums accepted; up to 4 completed works per artist, open internationally. Selected artists receive professional exhibition photography, a curatorial text, and installation support; 25% commission on sales, and the fee helps keep Duplex's studio rents below market for local artists. Exhibition September 16–23, 2026. — Deadline: July 24, 2026. Fee: €25. Prize: Group exhibition in Lisbon.

item.title: FineArt Igualada 2027 — Open Call
item.description: Open call to select the exhibition projects for the 15th edition of FineArt Igualada, the Catalan photography festival that turns the city near Barcelona into a large space dedicated to photography each spring. Photographers, collectives, and visual artists worldwide can propose a photographic project with a singular gaze — work that moves, provokes reflection, and opens new conversations through the image. Proposals are submitted by email; the festival runs February 19 – March 14, 2027 across venues in Igualada. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: The Shadow Aspect · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Open-theme exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis examining shadow as pure visual form and as psychological and cultural symbol — from formal studies of cast light to conceptual and metaphoric readings of the shadow self. All genres and processes welcome, traditional and non-traditional, analog and digital. Juried by Ann Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art. Awards include Juror's Choice (free entry into three future calls), Directors' Choice, and eight honorable mentions shown in the exhibition and online gallery. Images exhibited at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Exhibition August 22 – September 12, 2026; Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photo-Solo Exhibition Proposals — Season 23 · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest Gallery invites proposals for photography-related solo exhibitions to be held during its Season 23 opening period, September 25 – October 23, 2026, as part of the 2026 FotoFocus Biennial. Open to all artists working in photo-based media, including experimental and mixed-media approaches. Submit a proposal form, up to 12 images, and a resume; extended deadline June 21, 2026. Solo exhibitors receive a $100 honorarium, a free copy of the season publication, and automatic entry into the $1,000 Grand Jury Award pool; gallery commission on sales is 30%. A parallel all-media call for solo proposals across the full 2026–27 season shares the same deadline. Notifications by early August. — Deadline: June 21, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: Solo exhibition + $100 honorarium.

item.title: 21c Artadia Award 2026 — Northwest Arkansas
item.description: Sixth annual partnership award between Artadia and 21c Museum Hotels, providing $15,000 in unrestricted funds to one visual artist. The 2026 edition goes to Northwest Arkansas: applicants must be living and working in Bentonville or Washington Counties, Arkansas, and describe themselves as being at a pivotal moment in their career. The open call is free to apply and runs June 15 – July 15, 2026 via Submittable. Like all Artadia awards, funds are unrestricted — artists use them however they choose. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $15,000.

item.title: Southwest Artist · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe celebrating the spirit of the American Southwest — desert landscapes, indigenous cultures, borderlands, urban environments, and the region's singular light across Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Colorado, Utah, Nevada, and California. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, who selects 26 images. The gallery covers professional printing on Luster paper, matting, and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px longest side). Exhibition September 4–25, 2026 with opening reception; post-exhibition sales split 50/50. $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10. — Deadline: July 23, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition + professional printing & framing.

item.title: Wild · Photo Artfolio
item.description: Global online exhibit celebrating the natural world — wildlife, landscape, conservation, macro, documentary, fine art, aerial, and experimental nature photography all welcome. Open internationally to photographers of all experience levels. Entrants must demonstrate ethical photographic practice and respect for the well-being of animals and their habitats. Cash prizes of $500, $350, and $150. $20 for the first image plus media fees for additional entries; no AI-generated imagery. Acceptance notifications by August 19, 2026. — Deadline: July 29, 2026. Fee: $20 + $5 media fee. Prize: $500 + $350 + $150.

item.title: POOLSIDE 2026 · Jag Gallery
item.description: Swimming pools as subject matter — Key West's Jag Gallery invites work in any medium, including photography, that dives into pool culture, pool light, and poolside life. Open internationally to artists 18+; up to 5 entries, maximum 40 inches in any dimension, no AI-generated work. Exhibition August 8–30, 2026 at the gallery with an opening reception August 8 and a simultaneous online gallery. Judge's Choice, three honorable mentions, and People's Choice awards; winners are invited to a dedicated 2027 group show. Sales split 50/50. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $35 per work. Prize: Exhibition + 2027 group show invite.

item.title: Life in Baltimore · The Peale
item.description: Open call from The Peale, Baltimore's community museum, for work portraying life in Baltimore. Open to artists 18+ residing in Baltimore City and surrounding counties. All media welcome — painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, sculpture, assemblage — as physical 2D and 3D works (digital work must be presented as physical output; no screen-based media). Work must be original, created within the past three years, and not previously exhibited at The Peale. Exhibition October 8 – November 5, 2027 at The Peale; works are available for purchase with artists receiving 60% of the sale price. $25 entry plus $10 media fee. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Abandoned Haunts & Curious Trappings · The Firefly Artists
item.description: Annual celebration of the hauntingly beautiful at The Firefly Artists gallery in Northport, New York, judged by Matthew Christopher, the photographer behind Abandoned America. Artists nationwide may submit work in any medium — abandoned places, forgotten objects, and curious relics are the territory; photography sits naturally at the heart of the theme. Up to 4 works, maximum 36×36 inches, all for sale (35% gallery commission), no AI-generated work. Cash prizes of $200, $100, and $50 plus honorable mention. Exhibition October 6 – November 5, 2026 in the gallery's historic Main Street building. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (first work) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + $100 + $50.

item.title: Kahilu Theatre 2027 Exhibition Proposals
item.description: Kahilu Exhibits invites proposals for solo and group exhibitions in the theatre's galleries in Waimea, on Hawaiʻi Island, for three 2027 slots: June 10 – July 25, August 5 – September 12, and September 23 – October 31. Open internationally to artists 18+ in all media, including photography. Up to six proposals will be selected. Kahilu handles installation, signage, and promotional materials; artists receive 60% on sales but cover their own shipping, with no artist fees or honoraria provided. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Lacawac Artists' Residency 2026 · Lacawac Sanctuary
item.description: Week-long residencies at Lacawac Sanctuary, a 550-acre nature preserve and biological field station in Pennsylvania's Pocono Mountains, for artists and writers whose work shows the influence of nature or the science behind it. Residents get a private bedroom in the historic Watres Lodge or Ice House, studio space in the Carriage House, and access to 9+ miles of trails and Lake Lacawac. Remaining 2026 sessions run July 5–10 and October 10–15; applications are rolling, recommended at least two weeks before a session. The residency costs $300 for the week, due at registration; participants provide their own meals and transport. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $10 application. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Budapest International Foto Awards 2026
item.description: Annual international photography award promoting professional, amateur, and student photographers to Budapest's growing art community, from the team behind the Lucie Awards and IPA. Categories include Advertising, Analog/Film, Architecture, Book, Editorial, Fine Art, Nature, People, Portfolio, and Special, with single images and series of 2–11 photographs accepted. Top titles are Photographer of the Year and Discovery of the Year, with cash prizes, the BIFA trophy, and a winners' exhibition — historically at the House of Lucie Budapest. Jury includes Hossein Farmani and BBC Wildlife's Sheena Harvey. Extended deadline July 8, 2026. — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: Varies. Prize: Cash prizes + BIFA Trophy + Exhibition.

item.title: Paralaje Magazine — Issue Nº1
item.description: Inaugural open call from Paralaje, a new quarterly contemporary photography magazine published in Spanish with English translation, in print and digital editions. The magazine aims to give space and visibility to Hispanic and Latin American voices in contemporary photography, though the call is open to photographers anywhere in the world. Submit a cohesive series of 5–8 photographs engaging memory, territory, the intimate, the everyday, and the many ways of looking at the present. Selected photographers appear in both the print and digital editions. Free to enter; submissions close June 12, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST. — Deadline: June 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in print & digital.

item.title: Images of the Shrub-Steppe 2026 · Boxx Gallery
item.description: Annual juried exhibit presented by Boxx Gallery and Cowiche Canyon Conservancy celebrating the shrub-steppe lands of Central Washington — the tenth Conservancy show at the Tieton gallery. Work in any medium made within the past five years and inspired by the shrub-steppe landscape is eligible, as long as it hasn't appeared in a previous edition; CaFE lists the call as regional to Washington. Accepted work may be shipped to arrive by August 27 or hand-delivered September 1, and must be for sale (35% gallery commission). Juried by photographer and 2022 Guggenheim Fellow Nancy Floyd. On view September 5–27, 2026, with Juror's, People's Choice, and Cowiche Canyon Conservancy awards of $100 each. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Three $100 awards + Exhibition.

item.title: FL3TCH3R Exhibit 2026 — Socially & Politically Engaged Art
item.description: Thirteenth annual international juried exhibition of socially and politically engaged art, founded in memory of designer Fletcher H. Dyer and newly at home at Fischman Gallery in downtown Johnson City, Tennessee. All 2D, 3D, video, sound, and performance documentation is eligible, with photography as its own category; open worldwide to artists 18+. Juried by Jessica “JB” Burke of UNC Charlotte, with Best of Show, two Awards of Excellence, and a slate of named awards presented at the September 4 reception. On view August 7 – September 27, 2026; late entries accepted June 24–30 at a $45 fee. — Deadline: June 23, 2026. Fee: $40 for 3 works. Prize: Best of Show award + Exhibition.

item.title: 82nd Wabash Valley Exhibition · Swope Art Museum
item.description: Eighty-second edition of the Swope Art Museum's annual juried exhibition in downtown Terre Haute, running since 1944. Open to current or former residents of Indiana, Illinois, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee with original work in any medium completed 2024–2026 and not previously shown at the Swope. Juried by Mark Pascale, curator in the Department of Prints and Drawings at the Art Institute of Chicago. More than $10,000 in awards, from $100 Awards of Recognition to the Grand Prize, announced at the October 2 opening reception. On view October 2, 2026 – January 10, 2027. — Deadline: July 10, 2026. Fee: $40 (members free). Prize: $10,000+ in awards.

item.title: Baltic Open Submission 2026
item.description: BALTIC's all-comers exhibition returns for its third edition, with up to 100 works selected for a major group show at the Gateshead gallery from September 19, 2026 to May 2027. Open to anyone based in North East England — professional, self-taught, or hobbyist, individuals and collectives alike, working in any medium, with no exhibiting experience required. One work per artist, submitted as images via Submittable by 10am on June 16. Selection panel includes artists Laura Lancaster and Rachel Lancaster; selected artists notified August 6 and announced publicly August 20. — Deadline: June 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at BALTIC.

item.title: OD Photo Prize 2026 · Open Doors Gallery
item.description: Sixth edition of Open Doors Gallery's annual open call for emerging photographic artists working within the first ten years of their practice. Open-themed and international — from documentary and street photography to collage, mixed media, and experimental lens-based work; collectives and duos welcome. Submit a project of 6–15 images with an artist statement. At least 20 shortlisted artists join a group exhibition in London in November–December 2026 (venue TBC), with works produced by the gallery and sold on a profit-share basis. The winner receives £2,000, an interview in 1000 Words Magazine, long-term mentorship, and an OD artist listing with an Artsy profile for at least a year. Additional awards include Judges' Picks, the InCadaqués Award — a solo presentation at the festival in Spain — and the AJ Page People's Choice Award. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: £17. Prize: £2,000 + Exhibition + Mentorship.

item.title: Underwater Awards Australasia 2026
item.description: Third edition of the underwater imaging competition run by DivePhotoGuide, Underwater Australasia, and UW Images. Nine categories — Sydney, Conservation, Australian, International Waters, Tough TG, Portfolio, Smartphone/Action Cam, the new Only Water, and a Reels video showcase — with around AU$70,000 in prizes spanning dive resort packages, underwater imaging equipment, and a photography drone. Open worldwide; images must be shot in the Australasian region, with exceptions for the International Waters and select categories. Winners are announced at the Go Diving Show ANZ in Sydney in September 2026, where finalist images are displayed as metal prints; honours include a Scuba Diver magazine cover story and publication in the 2027 Australian Marine Conservation Society calendar. Proceeds support environmental partners. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $10/image. Prize: AU$70,000 prize pool.

item.title: ADEX Dugong Photo of the Year 2027
item.description: Conservation photography campaign from Asia Dive Expo (ADEX) and Asian Geographic spotlighting dugongs and their threatened seagrass habitats. Submit up to three images of dugongs in the wild or the underwater and coastal environments linked to them, each with a short story of 80–150 words; entrants also post their submission on Instagram with @AsiaDiveExpo added as collaborator. Free to enter. The grand prize winner is hosted at ADEX 2027 in Singapore with accommodation covered, receives a feature showcase, and is presented at the Blue Legacy Awards on April 11, 2027; shortlisted photographers are exhibited at ADEX 2027, featured online, and receive digital recognition. Public voting begins January 11, 2027. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Hosted stay at ADEX Singapore + Exhibition.

item.title: 12th Regional Juried Photography Exhibition · Rehoboth Art League
item.description: Twelfth annual juried photography exhibition at the Rehoboth Art League's historic campus in Henlopen Acres near Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, on view January 8 – February 7, 2027. Open to photographers living in Delaware, Pennsylvania, Maryland, New Jersey, Virginia, and Washington, D.C. — members and non-members alike. Submit up to 3 works created after January 2025; all work must be for sale, with a 65/35 artist/league split. Juried by Andre Wright Jr., who also awards $500, $250, and $150 prizes. Opening reception January 8, followed by a gallery talk with the juror on January 9. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $45 ($25 members). Prize: $500 / $250 / $150 + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Solo and Group Exhibition Proposals · Rehoboth Art League
item.description: The Rehoboth Art League's Exhibitions Committee invites proposals for solo and group exhibitions in its 2027 gallery season at the League's campus in Henlopen Acres near Rehoboth Beach, Delaware. Open to members and non-members working in any media, including photography; artists who exhibited at RAL in 2024, 2025, or 2026 are not eligible. Solo applicants submit 5 works and groups 10, created no earlier than 2024, with an artist statement and CV. A limited number of proposals are accepted each year; selected artists are notified by August 31, 2026, and receive 65% of sales. — Deadline: July 27, 2026. Fee: $45 ($25 members). Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Portfolio Platform 2026/2027 · Midwest Center for Photography
item.description: The Midwest Center for Photography's online series-portfolio program: selected photographers receive a six-month feature on the MWCP website from October 2026 through March 2027, presenting a thematic body of 10–20 images with an artist statement and biography as a virtual gallery experience. Work is evaluated on the strength of the series rather than individual images. Open internationally to all photographers; visitors can view and purchase photographs through the feature page (50% commission). — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $100/10 images. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Mini Maxi Print 2026 · Galleri Heike Arndt DK
item.description: Open call for professional graphic artists worldwide from Galleri Heike Arndt DK's Berlin space in Friedrichshain, for an exhibition of small and large-format print editions opening October/November 2026. Eligible techniques are editioned printmaking — lithograph, screen print, woodcut, etching, drypoint, linocut, photogravure and similar — in editions of at least 3; monoprints, inkjet and digital prints, and photo-based images without a physically worked plate are excluded. Submit 3–6 prints per section. Free to apply; selected artists pay a €40 exhibition fee plus shipping both ways, and works must remain available for the exhibition period plus 12 months. The gallery produces flyers and a poster featuring each artist. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free (€40 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PRC Artist-in-Residence 2026
item.description: The Photographic Resource Center's Artist-in-Residence program gives two artists working in photography and lens-based media four weeks of dedicated studio space inside the PRC gallery, October 21 – November 22, 2026. Each resident gets exclusive use of half the gallery (about 400 sq ft), access to the darkroom, alternative process lab, and digital lab at Lesley University, a $500 stipend, weekly feedback meetings with the PRC Executive Director, and the opportunity to lead one public program. The residency culminates in a dual exhibition November 14–23 with a shared opening reception, artist talks, and professional documentation. Non-live-in: artists arrange their own housing, and there is no location requirement; collaborators may apply to share one slot. Fee $30 ($20 for PRC members). — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $30 ($20 members). Prize: Residency + $500 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Jentel Artist Residency — Winter/Spring 2027
item.description: Residency at Jentel, a working cattle ranch 20 miles southeast of Sheridan in Banner, Wyoming, for the Winter/Spring session running January 15 – May 7, 2027. Residents receive private accommodation, a separate individual studio, and a $300 stipend distributed in weekly increments to offset living expenses. Open to visual artists in all media — photography included — plus writers and composers. Applicants must be US residents (citizenship not required) aged 25 or over; full-time students are not eligible, and Wyoming residents have a streamlined application. Applications close September 15 at 12:00 noon MST. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency + $300 stipend.

item.title: Hambidge Center Residency — Spring 2027
item.description: Self-directed residencies of 2–8 weeks at the Hambidge Center's 600 forested acres in Rabun Gap, in the mountains of north Georgia, for the Spring session running mid-February through May 2027. Open to visual artists including photographers, plus writers, musicians, dancers, scientists, culinary artists, and arts administrators. Residents pay $300/week (the actual cost of $2,250/week is subsidized by the center); merit-based Distinguished Fellowships cover two weeks plus a $700 stipend, and limited financial-aid scholarships are available. Application fee $30, with waivers on request. Note: no cell service on campus and studios are offline — WiFi in communal spaces only. Applications open August 1 and close September 15, 2026. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Residency + Fellowship options.

item.title: Künstler*dorf Schöppingen Fellowship 2027
item.description: Residency fellowships at the Künstler*dorf (artists' village) in Schöppingen, Münsterland, Germany. Applications for the 2027 fellowships are open June 27 – August 31, 2026. Fellows live and work on site for two to six months, arranged by agreement and availability. Individual fellows receive €1,500 per month (minus roughly €100–200 for rent and operating costs); collectives — accepted since 2023 — receive €1,000 per person up to €3,000 total. Open worldwide to professional visual artists, authors, and composers with no restrictions on nationality or age. Juries assess the quality of previous work, the feasibility of the proposed project in Schöppingen, and contributions to the residency community. Not a production fellowship: there are no presentation obligations, though fellows may use the exhibition spaces. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500/month stipend + 2–6 month residency.

item.title: 2026 Regional Fine Art and Photography Show · Lincoln Gallery
item.description: Annual juried regional show by the Thompson Valley Art League at its Lincoln Gallery in downtown Loveland, Colorado, running September 11 – October 1, 2026, with photography as a dedicated category alongside fine art media. Open to artists living in AK, AZ, CA, CO, HI, ID, KS, MT, ND, NE, NM, NV, OR, SD, TX, UT, WA and WY. Cash awards for Best of Show plus first and second place in each category. Enter via CaFE by July 8, 2026, 11:59 pm MDT. — Deadline: July 8, 2026. Fee: $45 (2 entries), $10 each additional. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Here & Now · Still In Street
item.description: Open call from London street photography collective Still In Street for Here & Now, a one-night exhibition at the Photobook Cafe, Leonard Circus, London, on August 20, 2026, 6–10pm, accompanied by a zine. Looking for candid, unstaged street photographs shot in London between 2020 and 2026 — no composites or AI-generated images. Submit up to 3 photographs by email (under 1MB each) with your name, Instagram handle, and a brief description; one image per photographer will be shown. Free to enter; a £20 printing fee applies to selected works, and selected photographers keep their print and receive a copy of the exhibition zine. — Deadline: June 24, 2026. Fee: Free (£20 if selected). Prize: Exhibition + Zine.

item.title: The Analog Forever Exhibit 2026 · LightBox Photographic Gallery
item.description: Fourth annual partnership exhibition between LightBox Photographic Gallery and Analog Forever Magazine, celebrating photography's analog roots. Open worldwide to any style or medium — the sole requirement is that the work includes at least one analog element in the creative process, whether it starts on film, passes through a hand process, or ends as an analog print. Platinum prints, cyanotypes, lumen prints, gelatin silver, three-dimensional objects and assemblage all welcome; the artist's hand must be evident. Juried by Michael Kirchoff, Editor-in-Chief of Analog Forever Magazine. Exhibition runs August 8 – October 7, 2026 at the gallery in Astoria, Oregon; accepted works due August 1. Fee $40 for up to 5 submissions, $60 for up to 10. — Deadline: July 5, 2026. Fee: $40–$60. Prize: Exhibition.
